Job Description

This Opportunity

WSP is currently initiating a search for a Senior Environmental Scientist – Environmental Permitting & Compliance
to support our Earth & Environment Team in New York
. This position will support a diverse portfolio of energy, transportation, infrastructure, and development projects, with opportunities to work across environmental permitting, natural resources, and construction environmental compliance.

The successful candidate will be a versatile environmental professional with experience working in New York City and Long Island and comfortable supporting projects both in the field and in the office. Field responsibilities may include natural resource surveys, wetland delineations, environmental inspections, construction compliance monitoring, and coastal or marine field assignments. Office responsibilities may include preparation of environmental permit applications, technical reports, impact evaluations, agency coordination materials, and environmental compliance documentation.

Your Impact

Conduct environmental field investigations, including wetland delineations, habitat assessments, natural resource surveys, and construction compliance inspections.
Support federal, state, and local environmental permitting for projects in New York City and Long Island.
Prepare environmental permit applications, technical reports, impact evaluations, agency coordination materials, and compliance documentation.
Interpret permit conditions, environmental commitments, construction plans, and environmental specifications and communicate requirements to project teams and contractors.
Perform environmental inspections and construction compliance monitoring for energy, transportation, utility, infrastructure, and development projects.
Support coastal and marine environmental compliance activities, including field monitoring and coordination with construction contractors and environmental specialists, as needed.
Review construction work plans and method statements for activities occurring in or adjacent to environmentally sensitive resources.
Identify environmental compliance issues and work with project managers, contractors, and technical specialists to develop practical corrective actions.
Coordinate with multidisciplinary teams including engineers, planners, environmental scientists, construction managers, regulatory specialists, and subcontractors.
Provide technical guidance and QA/QC oversight to junior environmental staff and field personnel.
Support multiple projects and assignments depending on project needs, including a combination of office-based technical work and field assignments.

Bachelor’s Degree in Environmental Science, Ecology, Biology, Natural Resources, Environmental Engineering, or a related field.
5 to 7 years of experience in environmental consulting, environmental permitting, natural resource assessment, and/or construction environmental compliance.
Experience working on environmental projects in New York City and/or Long Island, with familiarity with the region’s regulatory environment and infrastructure setting.
Experience conducting environmental fieldwork, which may include wetland delineations, natural resource surveys, construction monitoring, or environmental inspections.
Working knowledge of federal, state, and local environmental regulations and permitting requirements.
Experience preparing environmental permit applications, technical reports, impact evaluations, or similar environmental documentation.
Ability to interpret environmental permits, construction drawings, environmental specifications, and regulatory requirements.
Strong written and verbal communication skills and the ability to communicate effectively with project managers, contractors, field crews, clients, and regulatory agencies.
Ability to work independently in the field while also collaborating effectively within multidisciplinary project teams.
Strong critical-thinking and problem-solving skills with the ability to identify environmental risks and recommend practical solutions.
Ability and willingness to work in a variety of field conditions, including construction sites, wetlands, coastal environments, and potentially vessel-based settings.
Ability to travel throughout New York City, Long Island, and the surrounding region based on project needs.
Proven commitment to workplace health and safety and compliance with WSP health, safety, drug/alcohol, and harassment policies.
Ability to work schedules conducive to project-specific requirements that may extend beyond the typical workweek.
Occasional travel may be required depending on project-specific requirements.

Master’s Degree in Environmental Science, Ecology, Biology, Natural Resources, or a related discipline.
Professional Wetland Scientist (PWS) certification or progress toward certification.
Experience with environmental permitting and agency coordination involving NYSDEC, USACE, NYC agencies, Nassau County, Suffolk County, and other applicable local regulatory authorities.

Experience supporting energy, utility, transportation, infrastructure, or development projects in the New York metropolitan area.
Experience with coastal or marine environmental compliance and monitoring.
Experience leading field teams or providing technical oversight to junior staff.

Tetra Tech is looking for an Ecological Clerk of Works
to join Us in Shaping the Future of Ecological Delivery.
We have opportunities available across Scotland including Inverness, Edinburgh and Glasgow.

Join our collaborative Ecology team to support some of Scotland’s most exciting renewable energy, residential, commercial, and infrastructure projects. This is an opportunity to play a hands-on role in protecting biodiversity while helping clients deliver projects safely, compliantly, and efficiently. You’ll work within a technically strong, multi-disciplinary environment where your ecological expertise, practical judgment, and communication skills will make a visible impact on project outcomes.

Purpose & Scope of the Role

As an Ecological Clerk of Works, you will provide day-to-day ecological supervision and monitoring on large-scale construction and development sites across Scotland. You will help ensure ecological mitigation, protection measures, and site controls are implemented effectively, while supporting contractors, clients, and project teams with practical, proportionate solutions.

The role supports a wide range of ecological services for renewable energy, residential, commercial, and infrastructure projects, including onshore elements of major wind developments, as well as onshore wind and solar schemes. You will contribute to compliant project delivery by carrying out site inspections, supervising ecological surveys, maintaining accurate records, and responding to unexpected ecological issues on site.

Innovation
